messages:
amy: Heads up — around 11:12 UTC we saw a burst of 95th-latency spikes across the ee2 serving pool. Traces are sparse for affected requests, making root-cause fuzzy. Noticed kernel-selector flipped to int8-optimized kernel mid-burst. Anyone already on this?

ben: saw it. GPU mem pressure peaked but not OOM. KV hit rate tanked from ~98% -> ~63% at spike start. Could be cache eviction + different kernel perf profile. :eyes:

carla: dashboards show prefix_cache.evictions/sec jumping x6 and prefetch_retries up. Throughput dropped ~18% at same time window. Link: https://graf.redwood/internal/d/serving/ee2?from=...

observability-bot: alert: missing-trace-rate > 20% (service=ee2, window=5m)

ben: digging into kube events and runtime logs now. Pulling pprof for a hot GPU node.

dmitri: quick note — we rolled a sampling tweak last Tue on observability that reduced trace sampling for high-QPS paths to 1%. If that landed in ee2 it explains low coverage but not metric deltas.

amy: can you paste the sampling change diff? we need to confirm whether missing traces are masking a perf regression or if it's instrumentation.

ben: snippet from runtime logs (truncated):
```
2026-03-17T11:11:57Z runtime: kernel-selector: selected=int8_opt version=v3.2.1 latency_est=32ms
2026-03-17T11:12:01Z kvcache: hit_rate=0.98
2026-03-17T11:12:06Z kvcache: hit_rate=0.63
2026-03-17T11:12:06Z obs: trace_sampling=0.01 -> 0.01 (applied)
2026-03-17T11:12:09Z runtime: prefetch_error=EVICT_STORM count=42
2026-03-17T11:12:10Z deploy-bot: rollout completed service=ee2 tag=canary-2026-03-16
```

carla: that prefetch_error lines look like eviction storms. When prefetch stalls, requests miss KV and downstream kernel gets longer runtime — that could hurt throughput and amplify latency for int8 kernel if it's more sensitive to cache misses.

amy: high priority mitigations: (1) revert kernel selector to prefer stable kernel for ee2 canary nodes, (2) temporarily increase trace sampling to 5% for ee2 so we can profile, (3) throttle prefetch to avoid eviction storms. Who can take these?

ben: I can push a fast patch to selector config to prefer kernel=v3.1.x-stable and pin kernel-fallback=stable for ee2 canary. Will send canary now.

carla: I'll adjust prefetch worker concurrency and backoff to reduce eviction pressure. Will apply to ee2 pool 1 first.

observability-bot: deploy started: config/selector-pin -> ee2 (user=ben) :rocket:

ben: canary applied to 3 nodes. early numbers look better — 95th-latency back down ~12ms. KV hit rate climbing to 85%.

dmitri: bumping sampling to 5% now so we get traces for the next 10m window. Also lowering log sampling for debug lines to make room in pipeline.

amy: nice. after the canary, do a full rollout if stable. Also file a follow-up to revisit kernel-selector heuristics: we shouldn't flip kernel strategy purely on short-term latency estimates when cache miss rates spike. Need to incorporate KV hit-rate as a selector input.

carla: adding a ticket: PERF-1228 "selector: factor KV hit rate into kernel score" and linking dashboard + pprof. Owner: carla.

ben: FYI the initial profiler snapshot (with sampling up) shows that int8 kernel path has an 18% tail amplification when miss stalls occur vs stable kernel. I'll attach flame diff in the ticket.

amy: lessons / observability gaps: (a) trace sampling was too aggressive — hid the regression, (b) our dashboards didn't surface eviction storms correlated to kernel flips, (c) rollout bot didn't annotate selector config change in the incident timeline. We'll address all three.

dmitri: creating follow-up tasks: OBS-487 increase adaptive sampling on high-risk pools, OBS-488 annotate config-change events into trace timeline, OBS-489 retain prefetch error logs at higher granularity for 1h after spikes.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: selector-pin -> ee2 (status=success)

amy: closing the immediate loop. Thanks everyone — follow-ups assigned. If anyone sees residual spikes ping here. :thumbsup:

ben: noted one small residual bump around 11:42 — spikes are minor and correlate with one noisy tenant on node-7. I've isolated that tenant and flagged to infra to throttle.

carla: removing canary overrides after full rollout, leaving selector change in place until we implement KV-aware scoring.

amy: thanks. filing incident doc and linking ticket list.

observability-bot: incident-1797654321 created (severity=sev2)
